//: The `assert` block below is the family test standard (PORTS.md card 35) and must not diverge between repos. The `url` list above it is EXPECTED TO DIFFER: it names the pages this repo builds. Lighthouse CI runs against the built static output (dist/client) so dev-server quirks never affect scores. The url list is EXPLICIT on purpose: left to auto-discover, lhci caps at 5 pages and tests a near-random subset. Listing URLs covers every distinct template and skips non-page stubs. Accessibility is a HARD gate (must hold 100); performance / best-practices / SEO are warnings so normal CI variance does not block a PR. Not listed, on purpose: /studio, /preview/** and /api/draft-mode/* are SSR-only and never emitted into dist/client; /[slug] and /journal/[slug] build zero paths with no Sanity project configured; the nine module routes under modules/ are staged, not built. Add a representative URL per template as a project brings those online. Run locally: npm run build && npx lhci autorun

collect.//: NOT staticDistDir. lhci's own static server sends every byte uncompressed, and on 2026-09-17 that hid a real win on stonesteps-50k: inlining the stylesheet took the home page from 88 to 99 in a compressed harness while CI's LCP stayed at 4.2 to 4.9s against a 4.5s gate, because the 435KB raw HTML (84KB gzipped) was two seconds of download at the mobile throttle. Production is Cloudflare and compresses everything. scripts/serve-dist.mjs serves the same dist/client with brotli/gzip and the deploy's cache headers, so the numbers here describe what a reader gets. Build first: this server never builds. /styleguide is deliberately absent, it is the visual suite's fixed-data wall and not a page anyone visits.

assert.//: numberOfRuns is 3 and assertions use the MEDIAN, not a single sample. With one run, largest-contentful-paint as a hard error measures the CI runner as much as the site: on 2026-09-06 the identical commit passed on staging and failed on main at 6779ms against a 4500 budget, on a commit that only touched a workflow file. A gate that cries wolf gets ignored, and an ignored gate is worse than none. Three runs cost roughly 3x the job time, which is the price of the timing assertions being trustworthy.
